rules.heading: How scoring works in Sushi Go!
body: Sushi Go! is played over three rounds. At the end of each round, everyone scores the cards they kept, then discards everything except puddings. After round 3, puddings are scored and the highest total wins.

rules.heading: Card values
body: Maki rolls: the player with the most maki icons scores 6 and second place scores 3. Tempura: 5 points per pair. Sashimi: 10 points per set of three. Dumplings: 1, 3, 6, 10 or 15 points for 1 to 5 or more.
Nigiri: egg 1, salmon 2 and squid 3 points. Placed on a wasabi, a nigiri scores triple. Chopsticks score nothing but let you take two cards on a later turn.

rules.heading: Pudding
body: At the end of the game, the player with the most pudding cards scores 6 points and the player with the fewest loses 6. Tied players split the points, rounding down. In a 2-player game, nobody loses points for having the fewest.

faq.q: How much are dumplings worth in Sushi Go?

faq.a: Most puddings +6, fewest −6, split on ties. There is no penalty in a 2-player game.
No. An empty wasabi scores nothing; it only triples the next nigiri placed on it.
